thread:
incident-bot: URGENT: page delivered to oncall. Severity: P1. Customer: Delta Corp (dedicated VPC pool: delta-eu-west-1). Symptom: sustained p95/p99 latency spike above SLO. thread_ts=1783005678

eric (oncall): got the page — I'm in. Seeing alerts for high tail latency on their dedicated pool. p95 ~ 2.3s, p99 ~ 8.6s for generation requests. SLO is p95 < 350ms, p99 < 1s.

jess (sre): logs look like KV cache misses spiking and many requests waiting on `kv_fetch` RPCs to the cache tier. Could be cache thrash or network congestion in that subnet.

amy (eng-runtime): confirming: metrics show rapid growth in active tokens per request and a backlog in the runtime queue. Continuous batching backlog is up, kernel latency per-token is fine. Root cause could be I/O to cache or per-tenant rate shaping.

luis (customer-success): Delta reports user-facing slowdowns across EU. They flagged support ticket #DEL-4321. They said this started ~20m ago after a deploy on their side, but they couldn't be sure.  Customer wants ETA and mitigation asap.

eric (oncall): timeline: 1783005600 ~ baseline, 1783005600-1783005650 spike starts, 1783005670 alert fired.

jess (sre): quick checks I ran: `redis` latency increased for keys in the `delta:` namespace. Sample stack trace from runtime worker: ```2026-06-10T12:01:23Z runtime-worker-5 WARN kv_fetch timeout after 200ms for key delta:session:abc123```

amy (eng-runtime): can we confirm which cache cluster serves delta-eu-west-1? If it's a shared redis we can failover. Nate, you on infra?

nate (platform): delta-eu-west-1 uses `cache-cluster-eu-1` (multi-tenant, AZ-redundant). I'm seeing network retransmits between nodes in az-b. Possibly a noisy NIC. I can try draining az-b cache nodes and failover to az-a/c. That will cause a short spike; we should coordinate.

eric (oncall): options: 1) failover cache nodes (nate) 2) divert Delta traffic to backup pool (shared-pool-eu) 3) temporarily enable local in-memory KV fallback for Delta in runtime (amy) 4) throttle or shed low-priority calls from Delta (not ideal)

amy (eng-runtime): we have a runtime flag `KV_FALLBACK_LOCAL=true` we can toggle for the delta tenant config to avoid external cache calls; it increases CPU/memory but cuts network dependency. It's a hot patch but fast.

jess (sre): recommend sequence: (A) enable KV local fallback for Delta (minimal blast radius), (B) if still bad, divert new sessions to shared-pool-eu and enable burst capacity on dedicated pool, (C) failover cache nodes as an infra corrective.

nate (platform): I can enable fallback and provision burst nodes in 90s. Failover will take ~4-6m and I prefer to do it only if fallback doesn't stabilize.

eric (oncall): amy, can you deploy the runtime flag for tenant=delta now? Need a deploy-safe toggle (no full restart).

amy (eng-runtime): issuing a config change to the control plane now: `PATCH /v1/tenants/delta/config {"KV_FALLBACK_LOCAL":true}`. rolling apply to the region. I'll watch logs.

incident-bot: config change recorded by ops-auditor:change-id=chg-98123 at 1783005752

amy (eng-runtime): initial logs: `delta-runtime-*-1 INFO kv_fallback enabled for tenant delta`

jess (sre): metrics after fallback: p95 down to 480ms, p99 down to 1.6s — improvement but still above SLO. Backlog reduced ~40%. Good signal.

eric (oncall): still seeing occasional p99 spikes around 3.5s. Nate, go ahead and provision burst nodes and open routing to shared-pool-eu for new sessions only. We want gradual cutover.

nate (platform): provisioning burst nodes, requesting quota bump. Should be active in ~2m. Enabling route: `route-policy delta -> shared-pool-eu (new_sessions_only, 10% ramp/30s)`

luis (customer-success): messaging Delta: "We're actively mitigating an elevated latency issue in your EU dedicated pool. We have applied an internal fallback and are routing a subset of new sessions to a healthy shared pool. We'll update in 15m. Apologies for the disruption." Want me to send now?

eric (oncall): yes please — honest + status + ETA. Use the statement above and note we expect stabilization within 10-15m.

luis (customer-success): sending now. Customer replied: "Thanks, please keep us posted — some users still impacted."

amy (eng-runtime): burst nodes came up; routing ramp at 10% -> 30% -> 100% over next 3 minutes. Watching telemetry.

jess (sre): after ramp p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 720ms. That brings p95 under SLO but p99 borderline. Backlog mostly cleared. Looks like cache failover to other AZ helped.

incident-bot: ALERT: new error cluster detected for tenant delta: increased 502 responses for short requests (rate ~0.4%). Logged at 1783006600

eric (oncall): 502s are probably transient during routing change. Any persistent 5xxs?

amy (eng-runtime): digging: 502s correlate with a small fraction of requests hitting model variant `gptx-q8` (a quantized shard) that had an OOM when run on burst small nodes. I'm disabling that variant for new routing now.

nate (platform): I see one burst node with high OOM counts — draining and reprovisioning. Scaling policy adjusted to prefer larger instance types for Delta traffic.

jess (sre): overall: p95 under SLO, p99 ~ 700-900ms but trending down. Customer impact: partial, some user sessions had degraded latency and ~0.4% 502 error rate during the routing change window. Severity remains P1 until stable for 30m.

eric (oncall): we're passing to monitoring for stabilization. I'll do a handoff to jess in 30m and mark the incident in status page. Action items: (1) write temporary RCA notes, (2) follow-up infra failover root cause, (3) create postmortem and liaise with Delta for change freeze until corrective action.

luis (customer-success): Delta asks if we can schedule a call with engineering leads. I'll propose a 1pm CET post-incident call.

jess (sre): handover plan: I'll keep watch and own the next 3-hour on-call window. I'll file INC-2026-DELTA-LAT-001 and attach the timeline. Eric, pass any logs or context.

eric (oncall): handing to jess for ongoing mitigation and RCA ownership. My notes: enabled KV_FALLBACK_LOCAL at 1783005752, routed 100% of new sessions to shared-pool-eu by 1783005968, disabled `gptx-q8` variant for delta at 1783006635, scaled burst nodes and drained OOM instance at 1783006701.

jess (sre): thanks. Next steps: (a) follow up with infra on NIC errors in az-b and remediation timeline, (b) plan queued cache migration for Delta to a dedicated cache cluster (delta-cache-1) to avoid multi-tenant impact, (c) schedule operational runbook update for tenant-specific fallback.

luis (customer-success): customer update queued: "We've restored traffic and applied fail-safes. We're investigating the underlying cache/infra cause and will follow up with a detailed RCA."

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-DELTA-LAT-001 created at 1783007045

jess (sre): marking severity P1 -> monitoring, reassign to oncall rotation for overnight. I'll produce a postmortem draft tomorrow with timeline + proposed long-term fix: dedicated cache cluster for Delta + stricter canary gating for tenant-side deploys.

eric (oncall): ACK, good work team. I'll update the internal warroom notes and add the artifacts (graphs, logs) to INC ticket.

luis (customer-success): customer responded: "Thanks for the quick response. We'll wait for the RCA." They appreciate the rapid fallback. :thumbsup:

jess (sre): closing warroom chat for now — continue updates in INC-2026-DELTA-LAT-001.

eric (oncall): handover complete.
